observations.observation_key: projsayre/sayre|SEC-02|secrets-audit-data-lifecycle|docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-14-dead-code-hygiene.md (full MD5, twice) and docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-15-secrets-deps.md:16 (partial MD5) — the credential file's content hash, not its content|v3-md5-file-identity-disposition
observations.target_asset: docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-14-dead-code-hygiene.md (full MD5, twice) and docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-15-secrets-deps.md:16 (partial MD5) — the credential file's content hash, not its content
observations.attempt: Explicit disposition of review's standing Warning 1 (audit-14-dead-code-hygiene.md:103-104's full MD5 of the credential file), per the coordinator's direct instruction to accept or require redaction in writing — independently re-derived, not accepted on review's account, and extended to the sibling partial-MD5 occurrence in audit-15-secrets-deps.md:16 review's warning did not itself name.
evidence: docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-14-dead-code-hygiene.md:103-104 renders the full 32-hex-character MD5 (`120176f8745e0b1706e2b0fd67aded8c`) of both `infra/.env` and `infra/New Text Document.txt`, twice, alongside their byte size and a byte-identity annotation. docs/audits/deep-audit-2026-07-31/audit-15-secrets-deps.md:16 independently renders the same hash truncated to its first 8 hex characters plus an ellipsis ("`120176f8...`"). Both independently confirmed present by direct read this session; neither was touched by any of the three redaction rounds (audit-14 is outside the AC-9 redaction set entirely — its own byte-pin is unchanged and the passing suite proves it).

MD5 is a one-way (non-invertible) hash: given only the 32-character digest, there is no known feasible method to reconstruct the ~5590 bytes of arbitrary file content that produced it — this is a categorically different disclosure class from SEC-02 v1/v2 (real characters of a real value, or an exact map from a real value's location to its name). No secret VALUE, partial or otherwise, can be derived from either occurrence.

The marginal reconnaissance value is narrow and second-order: it matters only if an attacker independently obtains a CANDIDATE copy of infra/New Text Document.txt or infra/.env (through the OneDrive-sync exposure vector the audits already disclose in prose) and wants to CONFIRM it is the exact version described, without reading the file's own content directly. In practice this adds little beyond what the rest of the document already discloses (exact env-var names plus "REAL"/confirmed-live framing) — an attacker holding a candidate file would see the variable names immediately upon opening it, with no need for a hash to establish relevance. The realistic residual use case (automated hash-based matching against breach/credential-scanning corpora, bypassing manual content inspection) is real but narrow.

The same hash also has legitimate, disclosed defensive value: it lets the repository owner or a future audit run confirm, without re-deriving this finding from scratch, whether the flagged file has since been rotated/replaced (a changed MD5 would mean rotation happened; an unchanged MD5 — independently reproduced by this stage in both the prior run and this one — currently means it has not). This is exactly the kind of forensic indicator security advisories routinely publish without that constituting a secret disclosure.

Disposition (explicit, per the coordinator's and review's standing request, independently re-derived rather than accepted on review's account): ACCEPT, non-blocking. Both occurrences remain as-is. This is not a silent pass — recorded here as its own observation specifically so it is not skipped by silence.
